headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: AutoGPT can write/execute locally while Authelia exposes broad network/OAuth surfaces, creating medium pairwise risks for leakage, injection, and cascading misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content and exposes an agent protocol/filesystem surface, while Authelia exposes OAuth/ForwardAuth and broad network egress. A shared file or forwarded auth payload could carry attacker-controlled instructions into AutoGPT. The interaction is inferred from docs only, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Authelia forwards untrusted content into a shared file or agent-protocol message that AutoGPT parses as instructions
IF AutoGPT is configured to ingest filesystem or protocol payloads without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared file handoff between the agents
Add a strict allowlist for AutoGPT input sources
Strip instructions from any Authelia-generated payloads
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and verification

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia can handle authentication traffic and has broad network egress, while AutoGPT can access the filesystem and run shell/subprocesses. If they share a workspace or credentials, AutoGPT may expose sensitive auth material through its outbound calls. No data classes are listed, so this is not high, but the filesystem/network combination makes leakage plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or credential store
IF AutoGPT is allowed to transmit file contents or context to external services
mitigations: Block AutoGPT from reading auth logs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT has shell, subprocess, filesystem, and allowlisted network capabilities; Authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/ForwardAuth surfaces. Their write domains can overlap through shared files, configs, or auth endpoints even though no explicit locking is documented. Because the profiles do not prove a shared mutable target, uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or config file
IF AutoGPT mutates resources that Authelia also updates via OAuth/ForwardAuth
mitigations: Serialize writes with an external lock
Run one agent at a time for mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit auth-related outputs that AutoGPT may consume through files or protocol messages, and AutoGPT is capable of acting on those inputs via shell/subprocesses. If AutoGPT treats Authelia output as authoritative, a bad auth decision or malformed payload can cascade into incorrect actions. The pairwise path is inferred, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF AutoGPT consumes Authelia output without validation
IF downstream actions are triggered from that consumed output
mitigations: requires-engineering: add policy checks before execution

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes, residency, or retention obligations are documented for either Authelia or AutoGPT, so a concrete compliance mismatch is not evidenced. The only relevant facts are that Authelia handles OAuth/ForwardAuth and AutoGPT uses filesystem and agent-protocol surfaces; without regulated data classes, the compliance pathway is weak. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise, but no specific mismatch is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent's workflow
IF one agent is deployed under stricter residency or retention rules than the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared paths
